description:
**This repository has no git remote, so CI has never run anywhere and the Kotlin port has never been compiled by anything.** Verified 2026-08-25: `git remote -v` is empty, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s android job has therefore never executed on any machine.

Everything Android-shaped here is consequently **unfalsifiable rather than false**. `android/build.gradle.kts` exists (AGP 8.6.1, Room, WorkManager, OkHttp) and looks right; nobody knows whether it compiles, because there is no JDK, no `gradle` and no `gradlew` wrapper on the development machine either. The Kotlin half of the conformance vectors is in the same position — written, never run.

**This is the tasklist that unblocks the most, by a wide margin.** A remote lights up Kotlin compilation, the Kotlin vector execution that `110` depends on, and roughly five rows of the environment matrix at once.

**Two things to know before wiring CI, learned across the portfolio on 2026-08-25.** First, GitHub Actions minutes are free for PUBLIC repositories and billed for PRIVATE ones, and the account's private-repo Actions are currently blocked — *"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased."* A private amphora would produce a workflow that cannot run, which is the exact failure this batch exists to end. Second, sibling repos are developed by chief, which merges branches into main LOCALLY and pushes main — it never opens a pull request. A workflow triggered only `on: pull_request` never fires under that model; vita's had never run for precisely that reason.

So: a remote is necessary and not sufficient. Wire the trigger to how the work actually arrives, and prove a run happened.
warmup: command -v java gradle javac || echo 'no JDK/gradle on this machine'

userStories.title: The repository has a remote, and the workflow fires on how work actually lands
acceptanceCriteria: A git remote exists and `main` is pushed to it. Until this is true, nothing else in this batch can be verified by anything.

The CI trigger matches how commits arrive here. Work is merged locally by chief and main is pushed, so a `pull_request`-only trigger would never fire — `push` on the default branch is the trigger that matches reality. State the reasoning in the workflow, since a future reader will otherwise 'tidy' it back.

The visibility choice is made deliberately and recorded: private Actions are billed and the account's private-repo runs are currently blocked, so a private repo here yields a workflow that cannot start. If private is chosen anyway, the workflow must not be treated as a gate until billing is confirmed working.
Evidence: a run id and its conclusion, quoted in the story notes. 'CI is wired' is not a claim this batch accepts without a run behind it.
userStories.notes: Remote `origin` -> https://github.com/danieldekerlegand/amphora exists and `main` is pushed (git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main = 2a9391713fc96bf5549db82d6625c4c2cbb908f0, identical to local main). Trigger is `push` on `main` + `chief/**`, plus `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch`, with the reasoning written as a comment block at the top of .github/workflows/ci.yml. Visibility is PUBLIC (gh repo view --json visibility = "PUBLIC"), chosen deliberately and recorded in docs/reference/continuous-integration.md along with the consequence if it is ever made private. EVIDENCE OF A REAL RUN: run id 33038526156 (push, chief/100-android-into-ci, head a84c63b), conclusion FAILURE after 2m4s. Per job: react-native SUCCESS (npm ci, check:control-surface, typecheck, build all green); ios FAILURE (swift build -warnings-as-errors: non-Sendable BackgroundSessionManager stored in Sendable structs NativeResumableTransport/TUSKitTransport); android FAILURE (gradle :android:assemble) - the first time Kotlin here was ever handed to a compiler, which is US-2's subject. Local .chief/verify.sh on this branch: PASS Swift build, PASS Swift tests, PASS TypeScript typecheck, SKIPPED Gradle (no toolchain) - 0 failures.

userStories.title: Kotlin actually compiles, on a machine that has a toolchain
acceptanceCriteria: The android job installs a JDK and Android SDK and runs a real Gradle build of `android/`. The first genuine compile of this port is the deliverable.

Whatever the build surfaces is FIXED or recorded, not hidden. A prior review noted roughly four references to unwritten symbols; expect the compiler to find those and possibly more. A red first build is the expected outcome and is a success for this story.
A `gradlew` wrapper is committed so the build is reproducible and pinned, rather than depending on whatever gradle a runner happens to have.

The story notes report what ran and what it said. 'Could not run' and 'ran and passed' are different claims and must not be conflated — that conflation is what produced this repo's three auto-verified merges.
userStories.notes: REAL COMPILE, REAL RUN: run 33039508625 (push, chief/100-android-into-ci, head 09eac78), android job conclusion SUCCESS. `./gradlew --no-daemon :android:assemble` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 46s (54 tasks); `./gradlew --no-daemon :android:testDebugUnitTest` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 26s with ConformanceVectorsTest.sharedVectorsMatchAndroidPort PASSED, StorageGovernorTest.reserveDelegatesToAllocatorBeforeReturningReservation PASSED, TusdIntegrationTest SKIPPED (no TUSD_ENDPOINT). This is the first time Kotlin here has been compiled at all. TOOLCHAIN: the android job already installed temurin 17 + the Android SDK; it now also runs gradle/actions/wrapper-validation@v4 (SUCCESS) before building. WRAPPER: gradle 8.10.2 committed (gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/*), distributionSha256Sum 31c55713e40233a8303827ceb42ca48a47267a0ad4bab9177123121e71524c26 and wrapper jar sha256 2db75c40782f5e8ba1fc278a5574bab070adccb2d21ca5a6e5ed840888448046, both matching services.gradle.org's published values; CI calls ./gradlew, not the runner image's ambient gradle (which was 9.7.0). FIVE FAILURES THE COMPILER FOUND, ALL FIXED, NONE HIDDEN: (1) kapt refused every suspend/Flow DAO query - added androidx.room:room-ktx:2.6.1 [run 33038526156]; (2) TusTransport called Call.await() at 4 sites, never written - added transport/CallAwait.kt, an enqueue-based suspendCancellableCoroutine bridge; (3) UploadWorker referenced AmphoraGraph with no import; (4) SourceResolver probed seekability with ParcelFileDescriptor.seekTo(), which does not exist - replaced with Os.lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET) [run 33039150462]; (5) CoroutineWorker.onStopped() is final and cannot be overridden - the stop path is cancellation of doWork's coroutine, so the flush+lease release moved into a withContext(NonCancellable) finally [run 33039150462]. Test-harness fixes: testOptions.unitTests.isReturnDefaultValues (mockable android.jar stubs), org.json:json:20240303 (org.json is stubs-only in android.jar), unit-test workingDir = rootDir (both ports read the same repo-root-relative Tests/Conformance/vectors.json), kapt room.schemaLocation (exportSchema=true was exporting nothing), and testLogging events so a run of zero tests cannot look like a run of forty. NOT CONFLATED: local .chief/verify.sh on this branch reports PASS Swift build, PASS Swift tests (44 passed), SKIPPED Gradle (no JDK on this Mac), PASS TypeScript typecheck, 0 failures - the Gradle result above is CI-observed, not locally observed. The overall run 33039508625 conclusion is failure solely because of the pre-existing ios Sendable error recorded under US-1, which no story in this tasklist owns; react-native SUCCESS, android SUCCESS.

userStories.title: A skipped check can never read as a passing one
acceptanceCriteria: `.chief/verify.sh` currently SKIPS a check whose toolchain is absent and still exits 0 — correct for a developer machine, dangerous as a merge verdict. A skip must be reported distinctly from a pass, and the run summary must name every skipped check.

In CI, a skip is a FAILURE: the runner installs every toolchain, so a skipped gate there is a bug rather than a courtesy. Encode that difference rather than sharing one policy between the two environments.
Counterfactual test: with the Android toolchain removed, the local gate reports SKIPPED (not passed) and the CI gate goes red.
Document the local-vs-CI distinction where a reader will meet it, so the next person does not re-flatten the two.
